change.title: pr-6
change.description: UX: show complete URL path if website domain is same as instance domain
change.author: Arpit Jalan

findings.title: website_name gets around the TL0 untrusted-field restriction
findings.body: `website` is in `untrusted_attributes` (line 109). That means `include_website?` returns false when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true, which is a TL0 user viewed by an anonymous visitor (lib/guardian/user_guardian.rb:58-60). `website_name` has no such guard. The method at line 153 is named `include_website_name`, without the `?`, so ActiveModel::Serializers never calls it. It doesn't check the restriction anyway. The result: for a TL0 user with a website, anonymous visitors now get `website_name` (the host, sometimes with the path) even though `website` is hidden. The template at user.hbs:66-71 checks `model.website_name`, and `linkWebsite` is false for TL0 (`isBasic`, models/user.js.es6:107). So the profile page renders the spammer's domain as text in a `<span>`, which the restriction existed to prevent. Fix: add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` (that also defines the `include_website_name?` filter, which checks presence), and delete the misnamed `include_website_name` method.

findings.title: Profile header shows the old website name after the user saves preferences
findings.body: The old `websiteName` was computed on the client from `model.website`, so the header updated as soon as the user saved preferences. Now the template reads `model.website_name`, which only the server sets. The preferences route edits the same model (`modelFor('user')`, routes/preferences.js.es6:6). `User#save` copies only `bio_excerpt` from the PUT response (models/user.js.es6:209-213), even though `UsersController#update` returns the full UserSerializer JSON (users_controller.rb:100). After a website change, the header pairs the new `href={{model.website}}` with the old `website_name` text. If the user adds a website where there was none, nothing shows until a full reload. Fix: also set `website_name` from `data.user` in `save`'s `then`.

findings.title: TL0/anonymous spec doesn't cover website_name, so the leak goes undetected
findings.body: The list `untrusted_attributes` here doesn't include `website_name`, and the TL0 user in this context has no website. So the test still passes while `website_name` is exposed. Add `website_name` to the list and give the profile a website, so the test would fail on the leak described in user_serializer.rb:153.

findings.title: Sibling-subdomain branch has no test
findings.body: The new tests cover the equal-host branch and the `ends_with?` branch. Nothing tests the same-label-count branch at user_serializer.rb:144-146 (e.g. `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`), or a website that is a different subdomain of a three-label host. Add cases for the path-shown and host-only results of that branch.

findings.title: Sibling-subdomain check treats unrelated hosts under a public suffix as the same site
findings.body: The branch compares everything after the first label. Under a multi-label public suffix, unrelated hosts match: forum `forum.co.uk` and website `evil.co.uk`, or forum `foo.github.io` and website `bar.github.io`. The result shows the full path, as if the link pointed at the forum's own site. It's display-only, but it undoes the point of hiding paths for third-party sites. A stricter rule, such as only matching when the website host is `www.` + the forum's parent domain, would avoid this.

contracts.action: Server-side `website_name` attribute added to UserSerializer, replacing the client-side `websiteName` computed property
contracts.before_after: Before: the controller computed `website.split('/')[2]` from `model.website`, so it was hidden whenever `website` was. After: `website_name` is always serialized, because the `include_website_name` method lacks `?` and the attribute isn't in untrusted_attributes. It is shown even for TL0 users viewed anonymously.
contracts.visible_effect: user.hbs:66-71 renders the globe icon and `website_name` text. For TL0, `linkWebsite` is false (isBasic), so a span with the host is shown.
contracts.failure_mode: URI parse errors are rescued to nil, so nothing is shown. Restricted users leak their website host.

contracts.action: User edits website in preferences and saves; the profile header reads `model.website_name`
contracts.equivalent_path: User#save PUT /users/:username (models/user.js.es6:166-217), with the response produced by UsersController#update using UserSerializer
contracts.before_after: Before: `websiteName` was derived from `model.website`, so it updated right away. After: `website_name` is only set when the user is loaded. `save` copies only `bio_excerpt` from the response.
contracts.visible_effect: The header shows a stale or missing website name until a full reload.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent stale display; no data lost.

summary: The PR moves website display-name logic to the server so the full path shows when the website is on the instance's own domain. The main problem: `website_name` isn't covered by the TL0/anonymous untrusted-field restriction (its `include_website_name` lacks `?` and wouldn't check the restriction anyway). Anonymous visitors now see the website host of TL0 users whose `website` is hidden. Second, the header no longer updates after a preferences save, because `website_name` is only set from the server and `save` doesn't copy it back. The TL0 spec doesn't catch the leak, and one branch of the host comparison is untested.
